notes: cProfile and sys.setprofile are separate passes; both perturb execution.
Only uninstrumented_median_s measures application wall time.
Eligibility is conservative adaptive purity policy, not the full Pystachy language subset.
AST-admissible sources have not been compiled by this profile-only tool.
source_feature_tags describe visible syntax; many tagged features are already supported by the full compiler.
Exact int/float types do not establish native value bounds, finiteness, or intermediate overflow safety.
Fixed-budget context coverage assigns one body slot per (caller site, signature); it measures coverage, not dispatch or inlining gains.
Static-known entry signatures are supplied by the benchmark; they are not runtime discovery.
Per-function cumulative times overlap and must not be summed for coverage.
The int/float stream fits a two-variant cache; region cloning alone adds no type-discovery evidence.

method: CPython orchestration and output construction are included in every application sample. Independent oracle computation and equality checks are outside timing. No type/hotness tracing runs during performance samples. Static types are supplied before observing values; its Python boundary retains safety/fallback checks. Shared host results have no timing thresholds.

type_resolution.adaptive_entry: Exact int/int and float/int types observed at the CPython boundary
type_resolution.static_entry: The same two entry signatures are explicitly supplied before observing application values
type_resolution.helpers: Unannotated numeric_step parameters are inferred statically from the typed entry and range loop in every native region

one_variant_phase_budget.interpretation: The first compiled int signature exhausts the fixed attempt budget; later floats remain Python. No eviction/recompilation is claimed.

report_kind: Compact evidence extract. Retains all timing samples, workload totals, function eligibility inventory and full selected numeric distributions. Other per-site distributions are omitted; tools/adaptive_regions.py emits the complete report.
